isItGENUINELYDECORATIVEONEVERYSURFACE_th.theTest: in every one of the 20, the glyph sits BETWEEN two independently-labelled runs of text that are already separate DOM elements, and the surrounding sentence is fully parseable with the glyph removed. No instance encodes a relation, a value, a unit, a range or a state; none is the only thing distinguishing two otherwise identical strings. All 20 are the same construct - the provenance chip's field divider - and all 20 are inside a .prov ancestor, which is also why one CSS rule paints all of them.
isItGENUINELYDECORATIVEONEVERYSURFACE_th.verdict: GENUINELY DECORATIVE ON EVERY SURFACE. aria-hidden="true" on the .sep span alone is the correct fix, and it is the fix G-99 routed.
isItGENUINELYDECORATIVEONEVERYSURFACE_th.theCaveatIAmCarryingRatherThanDropping: aria-hidden makes the glyph exempt from 1.4.3 as pure decoration; it does NOT make it lighter on the screen. A sighted reader still sees a divider at 1.856:1. That is the shell's deliberate hairline treatment (var(--sc-line-strong) is the line token, not an ink token) and it is consistent with the visual law's quiet surfaces, but it is a design decision this fix DECLARES rather than repaints - and the declaration has to stay visible or the number simply vanishes, which is the next item.

aFOURTHFINDINGFOUNDONTHEWAY_aGatingIndic.theCode: src/a11y-gate.mjs, verdict(): `for (const w of waivers) { if (!w.rule.startsWith("independent-contrast")) continue; if (!(summary.independentContrast || []).length) { reasons.push(...) } }`. The per-arm STALE loop above it iterates `for (const f of summary.independentContrast)`, so a group that has stopped firing produces no `f` and is never compared to its pins either.

adversarialReview_CP1: AGAINST MYSELF: probe_clip.mjs reimplements axe's candidate rule rather than calling it, so 'the clipping hypothesis is false' rests on my reimplementation being faithful. It is cross-checked the only way that matters - against axe's ACTUAL evaluated set by element identity - and the two agree: at reference, axeEligible 4514 vs axeEvaluated 4272, and every one of the 242 differences is named by class in probe_unjudged, with none of them a clipping case. If my clip rule were wrong, the unjudged list would contain ordinary text; it contains only punctuation-only glyphs and disabled controls.

AGAINST MYSELF: the merge-ref explanation would be a story rather than a mechanism if it rested on the timeline alone. It does not - the CI log states the checked-out commit verbatim, the two trees' token values are read at source with git show, and the current tree reproduces the PASS on the same Windows machine that produced the FAIL. Four independent legs.

AGAINST THE DISPATCH: the dispatch relays K2's open reconciliation as the thing to establish, and the answer is that the premise was wrong - it was never an environment disagreement. Reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome (DEV_PROCESS 3.2), and the underlying instruction still holds and is still being executed: coverage does overstate, by 244 elements, for a completely different reason.

RISK I AM TAKING: retiring both waivers empties the ledger, and an empty ledger is the state G-95 was in when the gate had never been tested against a real exception. Mitigated by keeping every shape assertion, by the declared-decorative ledger taking over the .sep population WITH its measured ratio rather than dropping it, and by the group-blind fix meaning the next stale entry cannot hide.

RISK I AM TAKING: adding refusal classes to a gate that must stay green on main. Both new classes are measured at their current values FIRST (244 and 0 respectively), and if a class cannot reach zero honestly it will be reported rather than pinned - DEV_PROCESS 2.0 says a permanently-red gate is a dead gate and 4.5 says report what IS.
